text:
The Nifty 50 closed at 25,030.35, up 2.01% on the day and 8.58% over the last five sessions, while Bank Nifty rose 2.27% to 59,086, marking a broad rally across the market. Advances (217) outpaced declines (271) in the Nifty 500, giving a breadth score of 67.3, which the system labels “HEALTHY”. The move was fairly wide‑based, with leading sectors such as Financial Services, Consumption, Infrastructure, Realty and Auto all in the “LEADING” quadrant.

Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) were net buyers, adding ₹13,749.82 crore today and a cumulative ₹45,960.02 crore over the past five days, while Domestic Institutional Investors (DIIs) sold about ₹5,968.70 crore. The FII streak is eight days of buying versus six days of DII selling. Options data show a put‑call ratio (PCR) of 1.65 for Nifty, indicating more put interest, and a max‑pain level near 24,700. The expected Nifty range is 24,720‑25,340, with resistance (“call wall”) at 26,000 and support (“put wall”) at 24,000. Bank Nifty’s PCR is 1.24, max‑pain around 57,200 and a tight expected band of 57,686‑60,487.

Look for the Nifty to test its pivot resistance at 25,244 (R1) and the 200‑day moving average at 23,999. A break above 25,244 could open the path toward the next target of 25,500, while a fall through the 24,000 put wall may pull the index toward the lower bound of the expected range. In Bank Nifty, the key levels are 59,495 (R1) and the 200‑day average at 56,639; a move past 59,500 would confirm strength, whereas a dip below 57,909 (S1) could signal a correction. Keep an eye on FII flow trends and any news on the upcoming RBI repo auction and Diwali‑season buying.
